title: refactor(ci): split lint/test workflows and optimize cache/parallelism
author: Ethan Carter
description:
Motivation: Our unified CI workflow has grown large and slow; lint and test stages run more frequently than necessary and cache contention is causing longer job times. This PR splits lint and test workflows, reduces redundant matrix combinations for packages that only need lint, and adds improved cache keys + parallelism tuning to reduce queue time and restore effective cache hit rates.

What changed (summary):
- Introduced .github/workflows/lint.yml and .github/workflows/test.yml, extracted lint/test jobs from the monolithic build pipeline.
- Simplified matrices: packages-only lint runs use minimal node/version combinations; full test matrix preserved for core packages.
- Cache hygiene: tightened cache key semantics (repo path + lockfile checksum + action-version) and added fallback priming step for cold caches.
- Parallelism: adjusted job concurrency and batching to avoid API throttling and GitHub runner queue spikes; added dynamic job grouping for large e2e suites.
- CI speedups: enabled restored action/cache hit guidance, and introduced conditional steps to skip heavy lint rules on trivial changes.

Migration notes:
- Consumers: No changes required for developers. CI ownership should verify the new lint/test job names in build monitors and notifications.
- Observability: New workflow names appear in dashboards; alerting rules referencing old job names were updated where applicable.

Checklist:
- [x] Split workflows and validate local actions syntax
- [x] Preserve existing test coverage for core packages
- [x] Validate cache hit improvement in experimental run
- [x] Update monitoring dashboards and alert rules

Related work items: ENG-5123, ENG-5189. This PR is part of the broader CI hygiene initiative to modernize actions, reduce flakiness, and improve developer feedback loops.
